text: River Monsters is a British wildlife documentary series produced by Icon Films of Bristol, UK, for Animal Planet. Hosted by angler and biologist Jeremy Wade, the show follows his global journeys to investigate large and dangerous fish linked to local folklore and reported attacks. The series premiered on ITV in the UK and became one of the most-watched programs in Animal Planet's history, as well as one of the most-viewed series on Discovery Channel in the United States. Wade, born in Suffolk, travels to numerous countries including England, Scotland, Cambodia, Canada, Germany, Spain, Colombia, Bolivia, Iceland, Norway, Austria, Greenland, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, India, Japan, France, Russia, Suriname, Brazil, Guyana, the Solomon Islands, Indonesia, Zambia, Malaysia, Nepal, The Bahamas, The Cayman Islands, Mexico, Peru, Uganda, South Africa, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Nicaragua, Mongolia, Ukraine, Botswana, and U.S. states such as Alaska, Florida, Missouri, Oklahoma, Texas, Washington, Illinois, Oregon, and Vermont. In its first season, Wade searched for piranha, goonch catfish (during investigations of Kali River attacks), alligator gar, wels catfish, arapaima, piraíba, and bull shark—all known to be potentially deadly and poorly understood. The show details the feeding habits, behavior, and conservation status of these creatures, and rebroadcasts with behind-the-scenes commentary from Wade are available under the title River Monsters: Unhooked. The second season began airing on 24 April 2010, with the first episode, "Demon Fish," premiering on Discovery Channel on 28 March 2010; it consisted of seven episodes and included visits to the River Congo and other remote locations. In the episode "Death Ray," Wade caught a pregnant giant freshwater stingray, the largest fish he ever landed, which later gave birth to two pups during examination by Wade and biologists. This season also featured the white sturgeon, Wade’s second-largest catch. The ninth season was announced as the final season. Featured animals include sharks such as the bull shark, which can swim miles up rivers and has been found breeding in freshwater, including in Australia and South Africa, where a record-breaking bull shark was caught in a river. In Argentina’s Paraná River, Wade investigated the short-tailed river stingray, which grows to 6 feet and delivers a venomous sting, leading to a battle that became his longest. In Zambia, Wade explored the Zambezi River after reports of fishermen disappearing, identifying the vundu as the deadly fish, a southern African species believed to be responsible for attacks and drownings, and found it beneath the Kariba Dam. In India, Wade investigated the sareng catfish, a sacred fish in Hinduism, which is believed to bring bad luck if harmed; he faced resistance due to religious restrictions and eventually returned to perform a blessing to appease the gods. Episodes include "Electric Executioner," where Wade caught a stingray; "Silent Assassin," where he landed a massive river stingray in the longest battle on the show; "River Monsters Goes Tribal," where he reeled in a full-grown shark barehanded; "Freshwater Shark," which revealed bull sharks breed in rivers; and "Hidden Predator," where he caught a large bull shark in a populated river. Other featured animals include the Japanese giant salamander, white sturgeon, taimen, New Zealand longfin eel, candiru, and the giant snakehead. Wade also encountered the sea lamprey in Lake Champlain, where he used himself as bait and later caught them with a native tribe in the Pacific Northwest. The series also covers encounters with the electric eel, red-bellied piranha, tiger sorubim, golden dorado, arapaima, piraiba, black caiman, green anaconda, and various catfish species. Episodes such as "Jungle Killer" involved a lightning strike in Suriname, "Amazon Assassins" included catching a 150 lb arapaima, and "American Killers" featured catches of blue and channel catfish in Oklahoma. Wade also faced challenges with the giant snakehead in Thailand using a hand-made spear gun and encountered crocodiles and hippos in Rift Valley. The show includes a wide range of species such as the Greenland shark, European eel, Atlantic cod, Arctic char, and various fish from the Pacific and Atlantic regions. The ninth season was confirmed as the final season of the series.

Promoted as a special season under the title River Monsters: Mysteries of the Ocean, this season sees Jeremy Wade shift his focus from freshwater to oceanic fish. Featured animals include Fang's puffer, Asian redtail catfish, Mekong giant catfish, giant barb, giant snakehead, Cantor's giant softshell turtle, Xenacanthus, alligator gar, Xiphactinus, Indo-Pacific sailfish, Leedsichthys, whale shark, Megapiranha, red bellied piranha, Helicoprion, Dunkleosteus, white sturgeon, Rhizodus, saltwater crocodile, Pacific halibut, Chinook salmon, salmon shark, China rockfish, lingcod, giant mottled eel, giant trevally, narrow-barred Spanish mackerel, spot-fin porcupinefish, bull shark, saltwater crocodile, African tigerfish, blackspotted squeaker, humpback largemouth, vundu catfish, Nile crocodile, African fish eagle, Salp, Common ling, European conger, Moray eel, Atlantic horseshoe crab, Stomatopoda, Giant oarfish, Great barracuda, Pacific cubera snapper, Lemon shark, Southern stingray, skipjack tuna, Mahi-mahi, barracuda, snoek, bluntnose sixgill shark, oceanic whitetip shark, tiger shark, cookiecutter shark, brown fur seal, dolphin, isopod, pig, Greenland shark, Atlantic cod, Atlantic halibut, Rose fish, Cusk, dog, seagull, black marlin, needlefish, Bluespotted stingray, Goonch catfish, golden mahseer, gharial, giant snakehead, golden snapper, Leopard coral grouper, barracuda, giant trevally, Papuan black bass, bull shark, Wallago leerii, arapaima, giant snakehead, pig, Asian water monitor, arapaima, river stingray, black piranha, redtail catfish, goonch, golden mahseer, dwarf snakehead, carp, Indian flapshell turtle, mully catfish, flathead catfish. Wade revisits some of his previous adventures and investigates the spiritual and mythological events behind them. Jeremy also revisits some of the many scientific projects he has worked with over his career and presents new information discovered since his time with the researchers. This season was dubbed "the final season", as it is the last season of River Monsters. The season only had one episode, "Jeremy's Monster Story". River Monsters had the best series premiere in Animal Planet's network history by delivering 1.3 million viewers. It was also its most watched regularly airing primetime telecast in over six years. The second episode of Animal Planet's River Monsters delivered a 39% boost in total viewers (1.866 million) compared to the series premiere. Those numbers made it the best performing regularly scheduled primetime telecast in Animal Planet's history. The first season of River Monsters made it the best performing show in Animal Planet's history with every episode averaging over 1 million households. The season finale delivered about 1.47 million households. The second season premiere episode became the network's best season premiere ever. It drew in 1.7 million total viewers.
